QA: AWS SAA Study Notes

- Objective

Perform a targeted quality review of the changes made during the apply stage. Confirm that corrections were applied accurately, are supported by the corresponding verification evidence, preserve the surrounding meaning, and introduce no obvious regressions.

Prioritise technical correctness and exam usefulness over stylistic perfection. Minimise token usage and avoid unnecessary research or rewriting.

- Inputs
  Working notes: notes/edited/
  Verification reports: review/verified/
  Application reports: review/editing/
  Repository instructions: .github/copilot-instructions.md
  Git diff for the changes made during the apply stage

Read only the files needed to assess the changed sections and their relevant context.

- QA procedure
  Establish scope
  Identify the notes files changed during the apply stage.
  Match each changed file to its verification and application reports.
  Inspect the actual diff. Do not rely solely on application reports.
  Check each applied change
  Confirm the change corresponds to a specific verified finding.
  Check that the intended passage was changed and the correction matches the verification report.
  Confirm the evidence supports the exact claim now stated, rather than merely a related or broader claim.
  Check that qualifiers, conditions, limitations, service distinctions, and important exam-relevant details have not been lost.
  Check that the change has not introduced ambiguity, contradiction, redundancy, or misleading wording.
  Check omissions and scope
  Confirm every reported applied change is present in the notes.
  Identify unexplained changes in the diff, including edits not authorised by a finding.
  Confirm unresolved, low-confidence, rejected, and manual-review findings were not automatically applied contrary to the apply rules.
  Check that original notes and unrelated files were not modified.
  Check surrounding context
  Read enough surrounding material to detect contradictions or broken explanations.
  Check whether a correction makes a nearby statement misleading or obsolete.
  Do not perform a general review of unchanged content unless a changed passage exposes a specific concern.
  Resolve suspected technical errors conservatively
  Use the matching verification report and its cited official AWS source first.
  If the evidence is insufficient or conflicting, inspect the relevant official AWS documentation or current official SAA-C03 exam guide.
  Do not infer that a service or topic is excluded from the exam merely because it is not explicitly named in the guide.
  If a concern cannot be resolved confidently, flag it for manual review. Do not silently rewrite the notes or change an earlier verification decision.

- QA outcomes

Assign one outcome to each applied change:

PASS — correct application; evidence and meaning preserved.
PASS WITH NOTE — acceptable change with a minor non-blocking issue.
FAIL — incorrect, unsupported, incomplete, misleading, or out-of-scope change.
NEEDS VERIFICATION — technical correctness cannot be established from the available evidence.
NOT APPLICABLE — no actual note change was made for the finding, where that is consistent with the application report.

Do not treat stylistic preferences alone as failures.

- Output

Create review/qa/[section-id].md for each reviewed section.

Keep the report compact. Include:

Summary
Overall result: PASS / PASS WITH ISSUES / FAIL
Number of changes reviewed and outcome counts
Any unauthorised file changes
Results table
Finding ID Outcome Issue / evidence Recommended action

Include one row per applied change. Keep passing entries brief; explain failures and unresolved concerns clearly.

Required actions

List only specific corrections or manual-review tasks. For each, identify the file and heading, explain the issue, and state the minimum recommended action. Do not make further edits during QA.

If no issues are found, state that the reviewed changes passed QA and identify the scope actually reviewed.

Do not overwrite an existing QA report silently.

- Restrictions

Do not edit notes outside of the section(s) you're reviewing, verification reports, application reports, or repository instructions.
Do not rewrite content merely to improve style.
Do not repeat full triage or verification across unchanged notes.
Do not claim that a source was checked unless it was actually inspected.
Do not claim full-project QA if only selected sections or changes were reviewed.
Keep findings concise and evidence-based.
Finish by summarising the overall result and any issues requiring follow-up.
